scope: Original 2017 WizKids Sidereal Confluence: Trading and Negotiation in the Elysian Quadrant, ten-page SC_Rule Book_061017_Web5 and original printed nine-species fact sheets including Faderan reverse. Excludes 2020 Remastered, expansions, and optional variants.
grading_standard: Correct = every actually asked material fact resolved correctly with summary support, no material contradiction. Partial = asked omission/unresolved part without contradiction. Incorrect = material contradiction. Context is not an extra requirement. Assess every substantive same-entry field; labels and formatting alone do not set grade.

answers.expected_answer: Trade, Economy, Confluence (share technologies then colony bids then research-team bids). Trading ends when all but one player are done; players may immediately invent or use other Trade abilities before Economy.

required_facts.fact: Trade then Economy then Confluence
Trade ends when all but one player are done
Immediate invention allowed before Economy

contextual_background: Other Trade abilities may also be used at this boundary; not separately asked.
Confluence shares technologies before colony bids before research bids; internal Confluence steps are not asked by phase-order clause.
source_references: Rulebook p6 Phases and Trade Phase

answers.expected_answer: Complete as much of the original agreement as possible. Lose 2 per undelivered card or octagon and 1 per cube or ship: 2+2+2+1=7 points. Scores may become negative.

required_facts.fact: 2 per card and octagon; 1 per cube and ship
Loss is 7 points
Score may go negative

contextual_background: With no agreed compensation fulfill as much as possible
source_references: Rulebook p6 Trade Phase, failed promises
answers.novelty: Binding promises, compensation failure and penalties

answers.expected_answer: The species-background economic card is a loan and returns at the end of the turn. The colony and research team lack player backgrounds and are transferred permanently.

answers.expected_answer: Both must be in play and in their owner possession, not on loan. Flip target and put spent card underneath; each can pay for one upgrade only. A renamed upgraded card is no longer its old name and cannot pay an upgrade requiring that old card.

answers.expected_answer: Announce total ships, secretly divide into colony, research and retained piles; any can be empty. Both bids committed before reveal. Reveal/resolve colonies then research, highest to lowest. Buy one legal card paying all five ships; minimum is an eligibility floor, not the price. Pass keeps bid; must pass if none affordable. Colony bids reveal simultaneously when ready; research bids reveal simultaneously after colony resolution. Equal bids: fewer cards of that type, then higher species tiebreaker.

required_facts.fact: Announce total ships then secretly divide colony/research/retained piles, any empty
Commit both bids before reveals
Resolve colonies before research, each descending
Buy one eligible card spending all five
Passing keeps ships and is forced if none legal
Each bid type reveals simultaneously: colony when ready, research after colony resolution
Equal bids use fewer relevant cards, then higher species tiebreak

source_references: Rulebook p8 Bidding

answers.expected_answer: All remaining cards currently at minimum bid 1 go front-side face up beneath their respective decks. Slide survivors left and fill empty right spaces from top of corresponding deck, without flipping; front side up.

required_facts.fact: Remove remaining minimum-1 cards
Put under respective decks front-side face up
Slide survivors left
Fill right spaces from matching deck top without flipping, front side up

source_references: Rulebook pp8–9 Bidding cleanup

required_facts.fact: Producer retains last-Economy donations
Octagon worth half; two large worth half; three small/ships combined worth half
Concrete total 3 points
No final tiebreaker
